chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man is found slain, then if there is found for him a complete limb from among his limbs, salat (prayer) is performed over that limb and it is buried. But if no complete limb is found for him, then salat (prayer) is not performed over him, and he is buried.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: One waits regarding the person afflicted with severe illness, the drowned person, and one struck by lightning, or one upon whom a house collapses, or a wall falls upon him. His ghusl (ritual bath) and burial are not to be hastened, for perhaps unconsciousness has overtaken him because of that, or he has become weak such that death is presumed of him. So when his death is confirmed, he is given ghusl (ritual bath), shrouded, and buried. But one should not wait with him for more than three days, for after three days there is no doubt concerning his death. This is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.السَّكْتَةُ: a state of unconsciousness or apparent lifelessness
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: was washed with the ritual washing for the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on funeral prayer for a severed body part, and how long should one wait before burying someone whose death is uncertain?
ai.summary: This report gives rulings on funeral treatment when only part of a slain person’s body is found, stating that salat (prayer) is performed if a complete limb is present. It also states that burial and ghusl (ritual bath) should sometimes be delayed in cases where apparent death may be uncertain, such as drowning or collapse, until death is confirmed, but not beyond three days.
